值得閱讀的理由

  • 揭開牛排切開時流出「紅色汁液」的科學真相，徹底破除大眾對牛排血水的常見迷思。
  • 深入剖析歐美偏好半生熟牛排背後的現代化檢疫冷鏈體系，以及歷史文化如何塑造出「熟度鄙視鏈」。
  • 從公衛環境、肉類消費結構與歷史文化脈絡，理解華人習慣全熟飲食的深層原因，重塑飲食自主與自信。

摘要

破解牛排血水迷思與熟度認知的落差

作者指出，許多人在吃牛排時看到的紅色液體並不是血液，而是牛肉肌肉中負責儲存氧氣的肌紅蛋白與水分的混合物。歐美民眾普遍偏好三分熟或五分熟，甚至衍生出批評吃全熟者的飲食鄙視鏈。然而根據大學測驗研究，一般受試者僅憑切面照片判斷牛排熟度的正確率只有約三成左右，顯示許多人對熟度的要求往往來自心理標籤而非精準感知。

冷鏈體系支撐與飲食階級文化的成形

作者分析，歐美能夠安心享用半生熟牛排，仰賴的是其發展百年的現代化養殖、檢疫與冷鏈風控系統；加上原切牛排內部基本無菌，只要將表面徹底煎熟就能大幅降低感染風險。此外，這股半生食風潮深受法國美食文化推波助瀾，歐洲上流階層將食材原味與生食包裝成「高級」與「內行」的象徵，導致吃全熟牛排被貼上不懂品味的負面標籤，連前美國總統川普偏愛全熟配番茄醬都曾遭受菁英輿論諷刺。

中式熟食文化的歷史基因與肉類結構

相較之下，華人社會對熟食的堅持具有深厚的歷史與公衛背景。作者引用古籍說明，自鑽木取火以來「熟食避病」便刻入了飲食基因，甚至曾作為文明程度的象徵。加上華人傳統主食肉類以豬肉和雞肉為主，這類肉品潛藏寄生蟲與沙門氏菌等高風險致病原，必須徹底煮透以確保安全，加上冷鏈技術是近數十年才普及，因而形成了根深蒂固的安全防禦習慣。

回歸個人喜好：吃全熟從來不丟人

作者強調，牛排吃全熟完全不丟人。飲食的本質在於守住食品安全衛生的底線，其餘皆屬個人口味偏好，完全不需要以熟度劃分高低貴賤。中餐裡的東坡肉、醬牛肉等傳奇料理，正是將肉品完全做熟並兼顧美味的極致功夫；能夠把全熟牛排做得鮮嫩可口，更是考驗廚師的真正手藝。

item.itunes:author: 财经不眠姐
item.itunes:summary:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_cQejFlKFLY

值得閱讀的理由

  • 了解上門維修常見的收費套路，避免低價預約後遭遇層層加價。
  • 看見維修平台、師傅與消費者之間的利益關係，理解亂象背後的成因。
  • 掌握詢價、確認費用與保留證據等實用方法，降低維修消費風險。

摘要

維修需求增加，消費者卻難辨真假

作者指出，隨著房屋與家電逐漸老化，家庭維修需求不斷攀升，互聯網派單平台也隨之發展。然而，家電維修不像叫車服務那樣容易標準化，消費者通常缺乏專業知識，難以判斷故障原因與報價是否合理，因此容易陷入資訊不對稱與消費糾紛。

低價引流、誇大故障與模糊報價

作者整理出多種常見套路：先以低價預約費吸引消費者下單，師傅到場後再以檢測、耗材等名目加價；把簡單故障說成嚴重問題，藉此推銷昂貴維修或更換零件；也有人在防水補漏時只報每斤灌膠的單價，卻不說明施工總量，最後累積出數千至上萬元的帳單。這些做法的共同點，是費用資訊不透明，讓消費者難以在施工前掌握總價。

平台與派單機制如何助長亂象

作者進一步指出，平台抽成與派單規則可能加劇高價維修問題。當平台抽成比例偏高，且派單量與客單價掛鉤，師傅便更有動機提高報價、擴大維修項目。部分培訓也過度重視銷售話術，而非維修技術，甚至教導以配合演出的方式施壓消費者接受高價服務。

事前確認、過程留證，降低受騙風險

為了避免踩雷，作者建議消費者優先聯絡品牌官方售後；施工前逐項確認檢測費、工時費、零件與耗材費，並要求說明總價；維修過程中則可拍照或錄影留存。防水工程尤其要避開只報單價、不明確說明總價的按斤灌膠方式，改找具備資質的本地正規公司報價。

平台應負起把關責任

作者認為，若平台向消費者收取服務費，就應清楚列出帳單並加強管理，扶持服務可靠的師傅、淘汰亂收費者。唯有讓市場回歸手藝與口碑競爭，使消費者放心下單、誠信師傅獲得合理報酬，維修產業才能長久發展。

為了避免踩雷，作者建議消費者優先聯絡品牌官方售後；施工前逐項確認檢測費、工時費、零件與耗材費，並要求說明總價；維修過程中則可拍照或錄影留存。防水工程尤其要避開只報單價、不明確說明總價的按斤灌膠方式，改找具備資質的本地正規公司報價。

作者認為，若平台向消費者收取服務費，就應清楚列出帳單並加強管理，扶持服務可靠的師傅、淘汰亂收費者。唯有讓市場回歸手藝與口碑競爭，使消費者放心下單、誠信師傅獲得合理報酬，維修產業才能長久發展。

摘要

葡萄酒熱潮與高級形象的形成

作者指出，中國葡萄酒市場曾經歷狂熱時期，銷量高峰時，一瓶1982年拉菲甚至被炒至十萬元人民幣，名人也紛紛收購法國酒莊。葡萄酒的高級形象，部分來自波爾多酒莊分級制度所建立的名氣與稀缺性，並由此形成高價定位。

早年葡萄酒在中國走紅，除了張裕、長城等品牌推出平價乾紅，讓產品更普及，也受惠於加入WTO後進口關稅下降。當時業者還以美容、保健等說法推廣葡萄酒，進一步帶動消費熱度。

市場暴跌的原因

作者表示，中國葡萄酒消費長期依賴公務與商務宴請、送禮等場合，並不像歐美市場那樣普遍作為日常佐餐飲品。2012年起，隨著「八項規定」整頓公款吃喝，相關消費場景萎縮，葡萄酒銷量也受到明顯衝擊。

另一個障礙是口感與大眾習慣不合。乾紅中的單寧帶有酸澀、苦味，品飲也有一定門檻；若一味強調「不甜、苦澀才高級」，反而讓許多消費者難以接受，阻礙葡萄酒進入日常餐桌。

價格混亂與假酒問題則進一步消耗市場信任。酒商以遠高於實際售價的「掃碼價」營造價值感，也有業者將散裝原酒進口後在國內灌裝，冒充高價原瓶進口酒；假冒名酒屢次曝光，讓消費者對整個品類都產生疑慮。

高端定位的局限

作者總結，中國葡萄酒銷量已從高點下跌超過七成，一年少喝十七億多瓶。這場衰退反映出，若一個品類過度倚賴高端人設、品飲門檻與特定宴請場景，卻未能建立大眾日常消費習慣，當原有支撐消失時，市場便容易迅速萎縮。影片最後，作者向觀眾道別，並邀請大家點讚、關注。

值得閱讀的理由

  • 揭示爆款美食背後的行銷套路，解析「超長蛋塔」如何透過社群視覺衝擊轉化為消費者的社交貨幣。
  • 深入探討烘焙產業光鮮外表下的殘酷現實，了解為何每年倒閉超過十萬家門市的高淘汰率原因。
  • 分析消費者飲食文化、產品同質化與高毛利低性價比等結構性問題，提供餐飲市場趨勢的精闢觀察。

摘要

超長蛋塔引發狂潮與烘焙業倒閉潮

作者指出，近來一款長達60公分的超長蛋塔成為市場上的現象級爆款，不僅引發消費者大排長龍，更在短時間內創下單月銷量破千萬顆、相關話題播放量達數十億次的驚人紀錄。然而，在這股看似蓬勃發展的熱潮背後，烘焙業卻正面臨著極為殘酷的現實。數據顯示，在過去一年中，全國門市淨增長為負十萬家，平均每新開一家門市，就有高達36家烘焙店倒閉，產業陷入前所未有的「地獄模式」。

爆款產品的流量密碼與短暫生命週期

超長蛋塔最早由河南品牌透過線上直播推廣，隨後包括鮑師傅在內的各大連鎖品牌迅速跟進。作者分析，這類產品之所以暢銷，關鍵不在於口味有多獨特，而是其巨大尺寸所帶來的視覺衝擊，成功化身為年輕人的社交貨幣。但這種依賴流量的爆款模式往往壽命極短，從過去的髒髒包、黃油米糕到現今的巨型烘焙，生命週期已縮短至數月甚至幾週，熱度退去後往往是一地雞毛。

巨頭殞落與烘焙產業的三大困境

不只是獨立小店，連克莉絲汀破產清算、麵包新語關閉三分之二門市，甚至知名網紅品牌也面臨規模大幅萎縮的困境。作者進一步剖析產業三大核心問題：第一，麵包在華人飲食結構中並非剛需主食，年人均消費量遠低於歐美日韓，然而售價卻媲美一頓快餐，導致性價比偏低；第二，行業門檻低且嚴重飽和，各大商圈高度內卷，極度缺乏實質競爭壁壘。

產品同質化與追求流量的背後隱患

作者最後提到，烘焙業的產品同質化極為嚴重，只要某一單品走紅，同行便會在數天內迅速跟進。由於原料與供應鏈高度標準化，甚至連塔皮都來自相同批發商，單個蛋塔的原料成本低廉，毛利率看似超過50%，但商家為了搶奪熱度犧牲品質，導致消費者體驗不佳、負評倍增。過度依賴行銷與追求即時利潤，讓不少店家在失去產品核心競爭力的同時，也加速了被市場淘汰的命運。

摘要

結婚人數斷崖式下跌：數據揭示的嚴峻現狀

作者指出，民政部門公布的數據顯示，2024年上半年全國結婚登記對數僅為327.5萬對，相較於2013年同期的歷史高峰708萬對已腰斬過半，同時離婚對數卻呈現上升趨勢，相當於每十對新人結婚就有四對伴侶離婚。儘管官方強調要抵制錯誤婚戀觀並建設生育友好型社會，但年輕世代的結婚意願依然持續走低，甚至被預測全年度數據恐跌破600萬大關。

三大推手阻礙婚育：人口縮減、經濟門檻與社交孤島

作者認為，不結婚並非年輕人自私，反而展現了他們審慎評估撫養責任的成熟態度。結婚數下滑的核心在於三大動力：首先是適婚人口基數銳減與初婚年齡延後，從80後到00後世代人口大幅遞減，且年齡越大步入婚姻的機率大幅跌落；其次是成家門檻居高不下，高昂的婚禮花費、房貸與育兒成本讓近八成青年感到沉重壓力，加上大城市中超過五成年輕人成為缺乏社交圈的「孤島青年」，使尋找伴侶變得更加困難。

觀念轉變與政策鬆綁：婚姻不再是人生必修課

除了客觀條件的限制，現代青年對婚姻的價值觀也發生深刻變革。作者強調，婚姻已不再是固定的人生腳本，越來越多人將其視為順其自然或可替代的選項，單身也能擁有充實的生活體驗。為挽救低迷的登記率，政府在2024年實施婚姻登記新規，推行全國跨省通辦並取消戶口名簿限制，力圖簡化繁瑣手續以降低結婚門檻，但制度改革能否扭轉長期趨勢仍有待考驗。

================================================

3.275 million couples, a 7.5%drop,. hitting a new historical low—the. number of marriages has collapsed yet. again. Recently, the Ministry of Civil. Affairs released a set of figures: in. the first half of 2024, there were. 3.275 million registered marriages. nationwide, a decrease of 264,000 from. the same period last year, down 7.5%. Compared to the historical peak of 7.08. million in the first half of 2013, it's. not even half that. On the other hand,. there were 1.383 million divorce. registrations, an increase of 52,000. from the same period last year. What. does this mean? It means for every ten. couples getting married, four couples. are getting divorced. In fact, the. decline in marriage numbers didn't just. start in the last two years. Let's look. at this chart: in 2013, marriage. registrations reached a peak of 13.469. million couples. Since then, it has. basically been on a downward slide for. over a decade, falling below 10 million. in 2019 and below 7 million in 2022. In. 2023 and 2024, due to a post-pandemic " catch-up" marriage wave and adjustments. to registration policies, there was a. slight rebound, but it still failed to. reverse the downward trend. Some media. even predict that, given the first half. of the year is usually the peak period. for registrations, this year's total. might fall below the 6 million mark. If. this prediction comes true, it would be. more than just halved compared to 2013. However, not many people are surprised. by these figures. Some netizens even. joked, "It’s not that we won't marry,. we’re just delaying it. Those who are. prepared should marry first, those who. are capable should marry first, leading. others to marry later." Seeing the. number of marriages falling year after. year, the authorities can no longer sit. still. On September 14, the Director of. the National Health Commission said, " We must resist incorrect views on.

marriage and create a. fertility-friendly society." As soon as. these words were spoken, public opinion. erupted online, once again thrusting. the topic of "why marriage is becoming. less common" into the spotlight. Today,. we will combine relevant data and. research reports to discuss why the. number of marriage registrations is. dropping year by year. And what efforts. has the country made to encourage. people to get married? Let's first. address the first question: why are. fewer and fewer people getting married. each year? Some say the reason is that. young people are self-centered and. unwilling to take on responsibility. But does choosing not to marry or have. children mean one lacks a sense of. responsibility? The reality might be. exactly the opposite. As one popular. comment put it: I think today's young. people are very responsible. At the. very least, they know that if they have. children, they have the duty to raise. them, so they are carefully weighing. whether they have the ability to get. married and raise a family. This sense. of responsibility is a result of this. generation's upbringing; simply. attributing the cause to young people. being selfish is both irresponsible and. inconsistent with the facts. The. decline in marriage numbers is driven. by three main forces. First, there are. fewer people, and they are getting. married later. What is the number of. marriages primarily determined by? It. depends on how many people have reached. marriageable age. Data from the. National Bureau of Statistics shows. that there are about 223 million people. born in the 80s, 210 million in the 90s. , and about 163 million born after. 2000. Do you notice a pattern? Each. generation has tens of millions fewer. people than the one before it. The. current primary age group for marriage. is exactly those born in the 90s and.

after 2000. Since there are fewer. people, the foundation for marriage. registration has naturally shrunk. At. the same time, young people are. marrying later. According to census. data, the national average age of first. marriage in 2010 was 24.89, meaning. people married shortly after college. graduation. But by 2020, it had risen. to 28.67, an increase of nearly four. years in a decade. What is the pattern. here? The more economically developed a. city is, the higher the age of first. marriage tends to be. Take Shanghai,. for instance; in 2015, the average age. of first marriage in Shanghai was 29.7,. with men at 30.3 and women at 29.1. Delaying marriage means some people. marry a few years later, but there is. another problem: some people keep. delaying it until they don't marry at. all. Data on the probability of. marriage within five years for. unmarried people of various ages in. 2010 shows that for a 26-year-old. unmarried woman, the probability is. about 46%, but for a 35-year-old, that. number drops to just 5%, and only 10%. for men of the same age. A smaller. population base is the major trend, but. why are people marrying less and later? This has to do with the second major. reason. The threshold for starting a. family makes it impossible for some who. want to marry to do so. Let's talk. about money first; the cost of marriage. leaves many at a loss. A 2023 survey. showed that the average wedding. expenditure reached 330,400 yuan. What. does this mean? That year, the national. per capita disposable income was 39,200. yuan, and......it is over eight times. that amount. Note that this 330,000. does not even include the expenses of. raising a child. Young people. themselves know that these sums don't. add up. Another survey asked over 2,800. young people what exactly puts pressure. on them regarding marriage and.

childbirth. What do you think it is? Housing or rental costs, education. expenses, dowry or wedding gift. requirements—nearly 80%of people feel. that the stress of finding and keeping. a job is already affecting their dating. and marriage prospects. You see, many. young people aren't just facing a. simple question of whether to marry or. not, but a whole chain of problems: Do. you need to buy a house to get married? Does buying a house mean being tied to. a 30-year mortgage? Should the wedding. have dozens of tables? Should you have. kids after marriage? Who will raise. them? If the pressure mounts while your. income remains unstable, what do you do. ? Every question is followed by. concerns about money, time, and. logistics. It’s easy to tell people. to just get married first, but the. bills won't disappear along with that. advice. Taking it a step further, if. you want to get married, you first have. to meet the right person. Currently,. our country has over 200 million single. people, but the gender gap is a major. issue. The 2025 First-Tier City Youth. Status Report shows that over 80%of. surveyed young people in these cities. are single, with 56.8%categorized as " isolated youth"—meaning they have no. dates, no romantic interests, no. crushes, and no partners of the. opposite sex. For isolated islands to. connect, there must first be a bridge. If a person's life consists only of. work and going home, with weekends. spent catching up on sleep and a. shrinking social circle, where would. the opportunities for love come from? Are we really just waiting for a fated. encounter? Beyond the demographic. decline and the high barrier to entry,. the drop in marriage numbers is also. tied to a third reason: changing views. on marriage. Marriage is no longer a. mandatory life task. In the eyes of. some elders, life has a fixed script:.

study, work, marry, have children, and. retire. If you don’t marry, there. must be something wrong with you! Relatives take turns introducing dates,. and parents worry themselves sleepless,. feeling they can't hold their heads up. in public and will be laughed at,. unaware that many young people today. simply don't buy into that pressure. Hey, whose life is this anyway? People. spend their whole lives doing two. things: laughing at others and being. laughed at by others. Unless you have a. cervical spine issue, why wouldn't you. be able to hold your head up? That said. , young people today truly have more. options in life. Some focus on their. careers, some travel everywhere, and. some raise pets, living their lives. with great fulfillment. Emotional. support can also come from friends,. family, and other forms of. companionship; not marrying is no. longer equal to failure, but a personal. choice. Survey data from the report. also illustrates this attitude: nearly. half of the young people surveyed. believe marriage should follow its. natural course, neither forced nor. rejected; 41.4%feel marriage is a. necessary life task, while 8.9%believe. one can live a perfectly good life. while single. With the number of. marriages declining year by year, both. the central and local governments have. made significant efforts to encourage. marriage and childbearing. But what are. the specific measures? First, they are. making it more convenient to get a. marriage certificate. In October 2024,. the newly revised marriage registration. regulations were officially implemented. . These regulations did two things:. first, they upgraded marriage. registration from being. cross-provincial to nationwide; second,. they removed the requirement for a. household registration book, allowing. you to get your certificate with just.

an ID card. In the past, young people. working away from home had to take a. train back to their hometowns, bring. their household registration books, and. spend days traveling back and forth. Sometimes, melodramatic scenes would. occur where parents strongly opposed. the couple, forcing them to steal the. registration book from home just to. secretly get the stamp at the civil. affairs bureau. >> If I don't want them to get married,. they won't be able to—believe it or. not? >> I don't believe it. After the new. regulations are implemented, the script. will have to change. But is simplifying. the process actually effective? Perhaps. . In 2022, there were 6.83 million. marriage registrations, which rebounded. to 7.68 million in 2023. However, based. on the data from the second half of. this year, the outlook is not. particularly optimistic. Second, the. measures are quite direct: giving money. to reduce the burden of marriage. Multiple local governments and village. collectives across the country are. already handing out red envelopes to. newlyweds. For example, in Yuliang,. Shanxi, if both parties are first-time. spouses and at least one is a Yuliang. resident, and the woman is 35 years old. or younger, they can receive 1,500 yuan. in cash. Some villages in Foshan have. increased the stakes, offering. newlyweds a one-time reward of 2,500. yuan, with an additional 3,000 for. having a child. In Helan County,. families with zero bride price receive. 5,000, and low bride price families get. 3,000. The best one is Nanling Village. in Guangzhou’s Baiyun District, where. qualified couples can get up to 80,000. yuan, plus another 120,000 for having a. child, for a maximum reward of 200,000. yuan. Some think real money is great,. but others say these measures are just. a drop in the bucket. I think it’s a.

good start; it shows they see the. problem and are thinking of practical. solutions, right? After getting the. marriage certificate, what's the next. step? Raising the kid. So, the third. measure is to improve childcare. services so there's help with raising. children. By the end of 2023, the. number of childcare service. institutions nationwide reached 126,000. , providing about 6.6 million childcare. spots, of which 3.32 million were. affordable, public-benefit spots. If you really can't find. anyone, one parent is forced to quit. their job to take care of them. But if. affordable childcare can keep up,. family pressure could be reduced. significantly. Looking back at the. initial question, why are fewer and. fewer people getting married? It’s. certainly not just because "young. people have given up" or "lack a sense. of responsibility." It is driven by a. combination of factors like a smaller. population, financial issues, and. changing mindsets. Some are waiting for. the right conditions, some for the. right person, and others simply choose. to stay single. Pressuring people to. marry or using moral judgment won’t. work, so what is the real point? We. need to reduce obstacles and, ideally,. create better conditions. Truly. implementing the two-day weekend and. regular working hours gives young. people more time and opportunity,. letting those who want to marry find a. partner and afford a home, while. leaving room for those who choose to be. single. After all, getting a marriage. license takes a day, but building a. family is a life-long commitment, so. prioritizing quality is perfectly. reasonable. Before we wrap up, I’m. A-Jiang.
